command_or_fixture: WebFetch https://pypi.org/pypi/uv/0.13.1/json and https://pypi.org/pypi/uv/0.12.22/json (vulnerabilities array); read setup_index.UV_BOOTSTRAP_REQUIREMENT, _uv_install_env (UV_NATIVE_TLS set only when a CA var is present), and the two uv pip install command builders
counterexample_or_failure_condition: A fresh wf setup with no uv bootstraps 0.13.1 into the tool venv; setup_index._uv_install_env returns None in a plain environment (no SSL_CERT_FILE/REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE/SSL_CERT_DIR), so the following `uv pip install --exclude-newer` dependency installs (not hash-pinned) verify PyPI TLS against uv's vendored webpki roots, which include the compromised root. Because setup never replaces an existing uv, the vulnerable uv persists in that tool venv after later pin bumps.
expected: The pin decision records the known advisory and either selects a fixed release (>=0.13.4, with an explicit security exception to the 21-day package-age window or a short wait) or adds a mitigation (for example always using native/system certificates for uv), or the operator explicitly accepts shipping a known-affected pin.
known_bad_detection_method: Read the vulnerabilities array of the PyPI JSON the plan names as its own source, and traced setup_index._uv_install_env to confirm the plain-environment uv install path uses uv's default trust store.
limitations: Readiness review of a plan; no exploit was attempted. Not introduced by this wave: the current 0.12.22 pin carries the same advisory. Whether uv performs revocation checks that would block the revoked intermediates was not verified. The exact 0.13.4 upload date (and when it clears the 21-day window) was not fetched.
observed: PyPI JSON for 0.13.1 and for the current 0.12.22 both list GHSA-hq85-5cpj-mr62 with fixed_in [0.13.4]. The 22u25 plan states 18 wheels, none yanked, same tags (confirmed: 18 bdist_wheel, tags identical to the 0.12.22 table), and says no 0.13 change touches setup, but never mentions the advisory. _uv_install_env returns None when no CA env var is set, so the plain-environment path uses uv's vendored roots.
proposition: 22u25 pins uv==0.13.1, a release PyPI lists as affected by GHSA-hq85-5cpj-mr62 / PYSEC-2026-4321 (vendored webpki root bundle includes a compromised root whose intermediate keys leaked; fixed_in 0.13.4). The plan's evidence (changelog review, 'none yanked') does not mention the advisory, and its Decision Log does not weigh 0.13.4+ or a TLS mitigation.
public_path: wf setup -> setup_index._bootstrap_uv (pip, hash-verified, safe) -> uv pip install ... via setup_index lines ~749 and ~856 with env=_installer_env(_uv_install_env()) -> uv default TLS trust store
safety_and_authorization: Read-only: two public PyPI JSON GETs and repository reads; no files edited, no installs run.

disposition_rationale: do_now on the plan, not the code: the change exists to choose the uv pin, and choosing it without weighing a known TLS-trust advisory on setup's own download path leaves the decision unsupported. Repair is a bounded change-doc amendment (operator picks 0.13.4+ with a window exception, a native-certs mitigation, or explicit acceptance) before re-readiness; the other four changes are sound.

counterexample_or_failure_condition: The pinned uv is listed by PyPI under GHSA-hq85-5cpj-mr62.

The withdrawal and the new doc were written before this repair_start was recorded; this record is written before any further plan edit.

disposition_rationale: Real, in admitted scope; operator-decided repair: pin 0.13.5 with a window exception. Judgment kept from the cycle-0 finding.
